### A.3 Source register

{{SOURCES}}

### A.4 How this master applies Knowledge Once

- **Requirement text** lives only in Part D, as one record per requirement with a stable ID, source lineage, analysis class and exactly one disposition.

A bare `STG-NN` always names the executable procedure in Part E. Stage numbers and titles are the same in both places.
- **Stage procedures** (Part E) prescribe executable actions and cite requirement IDs; they never restate requirement text.
- **Appendix A** is the immutable provenance copy of the mandate, kept for authority and audit. It is not a registry; where a Part D record restates one of its operational details, the record cites the Appendix A line it comes from.
- **Every register and index** in Parts F–H is generated from the same records, so none is maintained by hand.
- **This candidate applies LXM-ACP-001 to itself:** `build.py` regenerates every derived view from the records (LXM-REQ-000223), and `validate.py` is the acceptance gate (LXM-REQ-000222). The candidate is not delivered unless every check passes. Requirement contributions enter this candidate only through `assimilate.py`, which discovers, classifies and resolves each one, validates the staged result with `validate.py`, and commits records and derived views together or not at all; refusals are recorded in `intake/exceptions.txt`. Its regression fixtures are in `test_assimilate.py`. Sources with a clause ledger (`sources/<SRC>.clauses`) are checked clause by clause for semantic coverage. A repository implementation of the assimilation mechanism does not exist yet; building it is STG-02 and STG-13 work, and its maturity is D2 *defined*.

## Part B — Canonical status model (LXM-DEC-000003)

One extensible model with separate semantic dimensions. A fact is always stated as a dimension and a value, never as a bare word such as "done". Dimensions and values are registered data, implemented on the repository's existing kernel lifecycle (LXM-REQ-000073); new values are added only by governed change, and existing values are never renamed.

| Dimension | Applies to | Values (in order where ordered) | Transition rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D1 Conformance** | each requirement | satisfied · partially satisfied · unsatisfied · blocked · awaiting owner decision · awaiting external verification · not applicable (reason required) | "satisfied" only with D4 = current evidence at the exact SHA; reverts when its evidence becomes stale or fails |
| **D2 Maturity** (ordered) | each capability, business profile, provider, method and technology use | conceptualized → architecturally supported → defined → implemented → registered and discoverable → configurable → validated → integrated → tested → verified → certified → approved → enabled → operational → production ready | each value needs its own evidence; an earlier value never proves a later one; "externally verified" means D2 verified with an external evidence source |
| **D3 Observation** | each gap-inventory item | existing and working · implemented not configured · configured not applied · missing · partially implemented · untested · externally blocked · awaiting owner decision | set by source inspection; reset whenever the code changes |
| **D4 Evidence** | each evidence record | current · stale · historical failed · superseded | becomes stale when code, generated artifacts, dependencies or execution conditions change |
| **D5 Release authorization** | each release candidate | NO-GO (default) · GO authorized | GO only by Bipin Kumar's recorded authorization, naming the exact commit and target |
| **D6 Technology lifecycle** | each technology item or release | discovered · candidate · under evaluation · compatible · verified · approved · resolved for a use · active · deprecated · rejected · prohibited | promotion to approved or active requires distinct-person approval (LXM-REQ-000045) |
| **D7 Decision** | each owner decision | open · packet prepared · decided (owner, date, scope) · superseded | only the owner sets "decided" |

| Technology lifecycle in SRC-0004/0006 and PR-053 | D6 |
| SRC-0006 §16 (fifteen maturity states) and §17 (seven requirement statuses) | D2 and D1 |

## Part C — Decision register

Every decision has three separate properties:
- **Status (applicability):** adopted (C.1, C.3) or open (C.2). An adopted decision is binding wherever its outcome applies, until a later owner decision supersedes it. Only adoption gives a decision force; an open decision decides nothing.
- **Normative effect:** what the decision fixed in this master. The *Effect in this master* column names it, and every record expressing it carries the decision in `k:`. Changing such a record is owner-reserved.
- **Mutation-authorization scope:** the *Authorizes* column. It lists the source clauses (and any records) that a gated change citing the decision may touch. *None* means an empty scope: the decision authorizes no change to canonical records. An empty scope does not mean that the decision is inactive, rejected, expired or superseded, and it does not weaken its effect.

## 1. What this document is

A destination plus enforceable rules. Every rule below has an **invariant** (what must be true), a **check** (how a machine knows) and an **enforcement point** (where a violation is stopped). A rule without a check is a principle, not yet a rule.

## 2. Constitutional invariants (first-class, never traded off)

| # | Invariant | Check | Enforced at |
|---|---|---|---|
| I1 | **Money integrity.** One exact money model: integer minor units, explicit currency and scale. Every movement goes through a ledger, is reconciled and is never inferred. | Money audit: no float money in scope; ledger balances | CI + runtime guards |
| I2 | **Tenant isolation.** No data, configuration or action crosses a tenant boundary unless a contract allows it. | Isolation tests per surface | CI + runtime authorization |
| I3 | **Security and authorization.** Least privilege, audited actions, secrets never in code or images. | Security suite; secret scan | CI + runtime |
| I4 | **Knowledge Once.** Each fact has one canonical home; everything else is generated from it. | Regenerate-and-diff; duplicate detection | Gate + CI |
| I5 | **Zero unjustified hard-coding.** Business, market, provider, brand and technology facts are governed configuration. Each exception is declared with a reason. | Configuration and code adapters (ratchet to zero) | CI |
| I6 | **Technology agnosticism.** Technologies and providers sit behind contracts and adapters; the core names none. | Technology governance gate; core scan | CI |

**Privacy and compliance** is not a constitutional invariant (owner's choice, 2026-10-31). It remains governed requirements (consent, retention, data ownership and jurisdiction, all by configuration) and release gate 19, so it still blocks release until evidenced.

## 3. The seven rules, made enforceable

| Rule | Final wording | Check | Enforced at |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 Connected architecture | Every domain declares what it provides and consumes. Cross-domain interaction goes only through declared contracts. | An undeclared cross-domain dependency fails | CI |
| R2 One source of truth | No parallel source of truth. **Transitional structures are allowed only if declared** (owner, reason, exit condition, date), are never authoritative, and are removed by their exit condition. | Transitional register: an undeclared or expired entry fails | CI + readiness |
| R3 Automatic propagation | A canonical change regenerates every dependent view, index, specification and test fixture. Nothing is synchronised by hand. | Committed generated files equal a fresh generation | CI |
| R4 Governed extensibility | New providers, markets, business models, capabilities and object types enter through **registered extension points** (contract + adapter + conformance tests). Generality is built when a registered need arrives, not ahead of it. | The core names no provider, market or business model; each extension passes its contract tests | CI |
| R5 No false completion | Each requirement and capability carries a computed state (§4). No state is declared by hand. | Readiness computes states from evidence | Readiness + release gate |
| R6 Automation by default | Every deterministic decision is automated. **Owner-reserved decisions** (financial policy, release, scope, irreversible data actions, security exceptions, architecture changes) are governed and never guessed. | Owner-reserved changes need a recorded decision with approval | Gate |
| R7 Enforcement at change time | Every change to knowledge, configuration or code passes the gate and CI before it lands. Independent assurance is periodic and never the maintenance mechanism. | Required checks protect the main branch | Repository settings + CI |

## 4. Lifecycle states (R5)

**Specified → Designed → Implemented → Configured → Enforced at runtime → Verified → Certified**

Each state requires its own evidence, and a state is never inferred from the one before it:

| State | Evidence required |
|---|---|
| Specified | A canonical requirement |
| Designed | A specification section |
| Implemented | Code traced to the requirement |
| Configured | A declared, governed configuration |
| Enforced at runtime | A runtime trace or an invariant check |
| Verified | Tests passing on the exact SHA |
| Certified | Release evidence and owner approval |

## 5. Layers (clarified)

1. **Foundation (kernel).** Identity, registry, configuration, rules, events, workflow, data, integration adapters, security. It names no business.
2. **Domains.** Commerce, Finance, Operations, Experience. Each domain owns its data and contracts, and invariants I1–I3 apply inside every one.
3. **Composition.** Business profiles assemble capabilities through configuration. A profile or template is never proof of a working solution.
4. **Intelligence (bounded).** Decision support and automation on governed data. It **proposes; it never acts** past an invariant or an owner decision. A change to production comes only through the gate.
5. **Execution and lifecycle.** Deployment, observability, resilience, recovery, automatic conformance.
6. **Knowledge and assimilation.** The Master and its gate govern every layer above.

## 6. Operating loop and order of work

**Loop:** Discover → Assimilate → Validate → Execute → Observe → Propose.
- "Learn" is defined as: measured outcomes produce proposals.
- Proposals enter through the gate like any other contribution.
- Nothing modifies itself in production.

**Order of work** (each step permanent, LXM-REQ-000230):
1. Invariants I1–I3 enforced for the launch scope.
2. The first-marketplace journeys reach **Verified** end to end.
3. Governance in CI: the Master in the repository, R7 active.
4. Generalisation through registered extension points as needs are registered.

# LXM canonical decision register. build.py renders Part C of the Master from it; assimilate.py and validate.py read it.
# Head line: @LXM-DEC-NNNNNN | status | group. Status: adopted (binding where its outcome applies) or open (decides nothing).
# Group: the Part C table that shows it. Fields, one per line as "key: value":
#   label short name; q question or conflict; o outcome; w adopted when and by whom; p approval provenance; r rationale;
#   f facts; opt options and consequences; rec recommendation (not approval);
#   e normative effect in this master; a mutation-authorization scope: source clauses (SRC-NNNN §n) and records, or None (empty).

ops: One entry point for all knowledge, a technology-agnostic contract, every version kept

All knowledge enters the Master through one entry point, the assimilation gate: canonical records, source texts, clause ledgers and every registry that holds a fact, such as identifier formats, actors, hosts, formats, vocabulary or thresholds. Nothing else writes knowledge, and a check fails on any knowledge that differs from what the gate last accepted. The entry contract is technology-agnostic: the kinds of contribution, their fields and the formats a contribution may be written in are registered data, so any tool or agent can submit in any registered format and any conforming implementation can judge. Every knowledge item is versioned: each accepted change gives it a new version, logged with its contribution, its time and the versions of the technologies that ran the gate; a change to a registry names the version it replaces and is refused if that version is no longer current; every earlier version stays reconstructable from the log. Every technology the tooling depends on is registered with the versions it supports, and the gate refuses to run on a version outside them.

# LXM canonical decision register. build.py renders Part C of the Master from it; assimilate.py and validate.py read it.
# Head line: @LXM-DEC-NNNNNN | status | group. Status: adopted (binding where its outcome applies) or open (decides nothing).
# Group: the Part C table that shows it. Fields, one per line as "key: value":
#   label short name; q question or conflict; o outcome; w adopted when and by whom; p approval provenance; r rationale;
#   f facts; opt options and consequences; rec recommendation (not approval);
#   e normative effect in this master; a mutation-authorization scope: source clauses (SRC-NNNN §n) and records, or None (empty).
# Status, effect and scope are separate: an empty scope authorizes no change and does not make a decision inactive.
# Only the owner adopts a decision. An adopted decision is never edited, only superseded by a later one.
# Table layouts: "%group | Header=key | ...". The ID column shows the ID, then " (label)" if there is one.
